entities.summary:
Zenob Glak was an Armenian historian and abbot who founded the Glak monastery in the Taron region of Greater Armenia around 450 CE. He is best known for creating the chronology that would become the History of Taron of John Mamikonean. This work has had a lasting impact on the study of Armenian history and culture, with many of its records still preserved today.

Glak's significance lies in his ability to document and preserve the history of the region, which was previously largely unknown. His work has been recognized as a crucial component of Armenia's cultural heritage, providing valuable insights into the country's past. The History of Taron has been widely studied and referenced in scholarly works, cementing Glak's place in the annals of Armenian historiography.

Despite the passage of time, Glak's legacy continues to be felt in the modern era. His chronology remains a vital source of information for historians and scholars, offering a unique window into the lives and experiences of ancient Armenians.

Zenob Glak's contributions to the field of Armenian history are undeniable, and his work continues to inspire new generations of researchers and scholars.

The History of Taron is a testament to Glak's dedication to preserving the cultural heritage of his people, and his legacy serves as a reminder of the importance of documenting and preserving our collective past.
